name: Efficient multi-scale decoders: BiFPN / EfficientDet (weighted bidirectional FPN), with FPN, PANet, Panoptic/semantic FPN, RevBiFPN and BiFPN-in-U-Net (U-Det) as comparators, evaluated as a replacement for the PretrainedUNet2d decoder
authors_org: M. Tan, R. Pang, Q. V. Le (Google Brain) for EfficientDet/BiFPN; T.-Y. Lin et al. (FAIR) for FPN; S. Liu et al. (CUHK/SenseTime) for PANet; A. Kirillov, R. Girshick, K. He, P. Dollar (FAIR) for Panoptic FPN; V. Chiley et al. (Cerebras) for RevBiFPN; N. V. Keetha et al. for U-Det
year: 2020 (EfficientDet, CVPR 2020); FPN 2017; PANet 2018; Panoptic FPN 2019; U-Det 2020; RevBiFPN 2023
venue_link: EfficientDet: CVPR 2020, arXiv:1911.09070 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.09070). Panoptic FPN: CVPR 2019, arXiv:1901.02446 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.02446). U-Det: arXiv:2003.09293 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.09293). RevBiFPN: MLSys 2023 (https://proceedings.mlsys.org/paper_files/paper/2023/file/c4f3fb058f957d5f753f9f9f0f08d991-Paper-mlsys2023.pdf). Enhanced YOLOv5 PANet->BiFPN ablation: PMC10611198 (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10611198/).
code_availability: Public: google/automl (official EfficientDet TF), rwightman/efficientdet-pytorch (PyTorch BiFPN, timm-compatible), zylo117/Yet-Another-EfficientDet-Pytorch; FPN decoders in segmentation_models_pytorch (Unet, FPN, PAN, UPerNet). No BiFPN code exists in the Erudition repo today (grep for BiFPN/FPN in kaggle_1st_place/solution finds nothing).
evidence_level: Peer-reviewed for EfficientDet/FPN/Panoptic FPN (object detection and 1/4-resolution semantic segmentation). No peer-reviewed evidence found for BiFPN beating a U-Net decoder on full-resolution dense regression (depth, disparity, or column-wise distributions). BiFPN-vs-U-Net evidence is limited to small medical-segmentation papers (U-Det, arXiv, non-pretrained baseline) and detection-neck ablations in YOLO variants.
extreme_summary: BiFPN is a detection neck: repeated top-down plus bottom-up fusion over P3-P7 with learned, normalised per-input weights. In its own ablation the weighted fusion adds only +0.45 COCO AP over unweighted BiFPN, and +0.31 AP over repeated FPN+PANet at 0.68x FLOPs. Its one segmentation result predicts at 1/4 resolution and confounds the backbone. Nothing here supports a lower RMSE for our full-resolution column-softmax output, and the only FLOP saving on offer (narrower mid-level fusion) can be had inside the existing U-Net.
task_definition: EfficientDet: multi-scale object detection (box + class) on COCO, with a secondary semantic-segmentation experiment on Pascal VOC 2012. In Erudition the analogous role would be the decoder that turns ConvNeXt/FastViT stage maps into a full-resolution 345 MD x 400 TVT feature map, which a per-column softmax over TVT levels turns into a distribution that is expectation-decoded to TVT.
inputs: RGB images for EfficientDet. In our setting the decoder input is the 4 encoder stage maps (convnext_small at 16ch 400x345, measured: 96ch 200x87, 192ch 100x43, 384ch 50x21, 768ch 25x10 with the default stem_stride (2,4)) plus the full-resolution stem skip (emb_dim 32).
target_parameterisation: Not applicable (a generic decoder). It leaves our target unchanged: a per-column categorical distribution over 400 TVT levels.
output_representation: EfficientDet emits box/class heads at P3-P7 (1/8 to 1/128). Its segmentation variant adds P2 and predicts at 1/4 resolution, then upsamples bilinearly. The Panoptic/semantic FPN head likewise merges levels at 1/4 and upsamples 4x. Neither natively outputs full resolution; our output has to be full resolution along the 400-level TVT axis, because that axis is the class axis of the softmax.
architecture: BiFPN layer: every level is projected to a single width W (64-384 depending on D0-D7). A top-down pass is followed by a bottom-up pass; nodes with a single input are removed, and an extra same-level edge runs from input to output at the middle levels. Each fusion node computes O = sum_i w_i * I_i / (eps + sum_j w_j) with ReLU-constrained scalar weights (fast normalised fusion), followed by a depthwise-separable 3x3 conv, BN and swish. The layer is repeated 3-8 times (compound scaling). Segmentation variant: levels P2-P7, W=128, 3 BiFPN repeats, classification head width 256 repeated 3 times, per-pixel classification on P2 only. For comparison, the current PretrainedUNet2d decoder (experiments/bilzard/seq_NN_pretrained_unet.py): 3 BilinearResUpBlock2d (bilinear upsample, concat skip, 1x1 proj to the skip width, ResBlock of two 3x3 convs) at widths 384/192/96. Then to_full_resolution (1x1 to 32), BilinearAddResUpBlock2d with the full-resolution stem skip, and an out ResBlock at 32 channels. Measured parameter counts (convnext_small, this session): up_blocks 3.10M / 0.78M / 0.19M, full_up_block 0.019M, out 0.019M, stem 0.015M. Each up-block level is about 3.3 GMAC. The three full-resolution parts are about 2.0-2.6 GMAC each, together about 34 GFLOP, which matches the 32.9 GFLOP 'other spatial convs (decoder, stem)' row in kaggle_1st_place/CLAUDE.md.
core_mechanism: (1) Bidirectional cross-scale flow, so coarse levels also receive fine detail. (2) Learned scalar per-input fusion weights. (3) Uniform narrow width with depthwise-separable convs, which is where the FLOP savings come from. (4) Repetition. For a detector, (1) matters because predictions are made at every level. For a single full-resolution output, the last bottom-up pass feeds levels that are never read, so the useful part reduces to a repeated top-down FPN with extra lateral edges.
training_objective: Focal loss + smooth-L1 box loss for detection; per-pixel cross-entropy for segmentation. In Erudition the existing column-softmax CE/KD losses and deep supervision would stay. Note that deep supervision is wired to unet.deep_sup_stage_channels (experiments/bilzard/seq_NN_models.py:613), so a BiFPN decoder must expose the same per-level feature list or deep supervision breaks.
decoding: Not applicable (the decoder changes features, not the decode). Our expectation decode over the per-column softmax stays as is.
metric_consistent_decode: Neutral: a decoder swap leaves the expectation decode, which is Bayes-optimal for RMSE, unchanged.
evidence_scope: Whole image (local-to-global via the pyramid). In our case the whole 345x400 cost image of one lateral. It adds no new evidence sources.
prefix_conditioning: None. Whatever the input channels already encode passes through unchanged.
propose_vs_select: Single output. A BiFPN-decoder model could be trained as a separate blend member, but its only source of diversity would be decoder topology.
physical_constraints: None. BiFPN imposes no ordering, smoothness or continuity.
dataset: COCO 2017 (detection), Pascal VOC 2012 (segmentation), LUNA-16 (U-Det, 1,186 nodules). None resemble our 16-channel synthetic cost images (85% synthetic training wells, 155 real holdout wells).
synthetic_to_real: Not addressed by any BiFPN source. The architecture has no bearing on the synthetic-to-real gap.
metric_and_performance: EfficientDet Table 5 (same EfficientNet-B3 backbone and heads, COCO AP): repeated top-down FPN 42.29 (1.0x params / 1.0x FLOPs); repeated FPN+PANet 44.08 (1.0x / 1.0x); NAS-FPN 43.16 (0.71x / 0.72x); fully connected FPN 43.06; BiFPN unweighted 43.94 (0.88x / 0.67x); BiFPN weighted 44.39 (0.88x / 0.68x). So weighted fusion is worth +0.45 AP, and BiFPN beats repeated PANet by +0.31 AP at about two thirds of the FLOPs. Table 4: RetinaNet ResNet50+FPN 37.0 AP (34M, 97B) -> EfficientNet-B3+FPN 40.3 (21M, 75B) -> EfficientNet-B3+BiFPN 44.4 (12M, 24B). Here the BiFPN step (+4.1 AP) also brings repetition and scaling, so the headline number is not a like-for-like neck swap. Table 6: softmax vs fast fusion differ by -0.01 to -0.11 AP, with fast fusion 1.26-1.31x faster. Segmentation: EfficientDet-D4-based model reaches 81.74% mIoU on Pascal VOC 2012 at 18B FLOPs, against DeepLabV3+ 1.7 points lower at 9.8x the FLOPs. The backbone and decoder change together, and the prediction is made at 1/4 resolution. YOLOv5 PANet->BiFPN: +0.8 mAP@0.5 (PMC10611198). U-Det (encoder + BiFPN instead of the U-Net expansive path): DSC 82.82% on LUNA-16, better than a from-scratch vanilla U-Net baseline [uncertain: parameter comparison not verified from the full text].
comparability: Low. Detection AP and 1/4-resolution mIoU gains of 0.3-1.7 points do not translate into a predicted ft-RMSE change on 155 holdout wells. The closest in-repo evidence is internal: the 2:1 resolution rule (2nd-place workspace: one extra halving cost 0.9 ft, two cost 1.7 ft) and the decoder-cost breakdown in kaggle_1st_place/CLAUDE.md.
validation_protocol: COCO test-dev / VOC val, single model, single scale. The ablations are clean for detection (same backbone and heads). The segmentation comparison is not controlled for backbone.
inference_budget: No new cost figures from the literature apply. In-repo timing (convnext_tiny, 345x400, fp16, batch 1, total ~22 ms): up_blocks ~5 ms, full_up_block 2.2 ms, out 1.5 ms, stem 1.8 ms. A BiFPN can only replace the ~5 ms up-block part, because the ~5.5 ms full-resolution part is still needed to reach 400 TVT levels. Realistic saving: 2-4 ms per forward pass (about 10-15%), against ~75-80 ms whole-pipeline cost per well, of which the U-Net is roughly a third. Repeated BiFPN layers with depthwise convs are memory-bound. CLAUDE.md already shows FLOPs do not predict wall clock here (EfficientNet-B3 slower than convnext_tiny at a quarter of the FLOPs), so any FLOP claim has to be re-timed with CUDA events. [uncertain: the 2-4 ms saving is an estimate, not a measurement]
repeated_layers: Not addressed. Band confusion (choosing or blending the wrong repeated band) comes from ambiguous evidence. The deepest stage (25x10 at convnext_small, 768 ch) already covers the whole image, so extra cross-scale fusion adds little receptive field and no new evidence.
drift: Not addressed. Slow straight-line drift per well is an evidence/prior problem, not a multi-scale fusion problem.
uncertainty_and_calibration: None. BiFPN has no calibration mechanism. Any change in posterior calibration from a decoder swap would be incidental and must be measured (e.g. per-column NLL / ECE on holdout).
where_to_use: Only as an alternative decoder inside PretrainedUNet2d (experiments/bilzard/seq_NN_pretrained_unet.py, and the copy in experiments/arch/), replacing the three BilinearResUpBlock2d. to_full_resolution, full_up_block (stem skip) and the out block stay, since the full-resolution TVT axis cannot be removed without breaking the 2:1 rule. Possible secondary use: the decoder for the FastViT-SA12 student, if it measurably cuts student latency at equal RMSE.
error_mode_targeted: None of the three main modes directly (band confusion ~51%, drift ~25%, broad hump ~13%). At best a small general feature-quality or latency effect. The teammate's 'lower RMSE' claim has no mechanism tied to a known error mode.
gap_vs_our_implementation: What we already do: the decoder is a bilinear U-Net with concat skips at every encoder level plus a full-resolution stem skip. That is a single top-down multi-scale pathway with lateral connections, i.e. FPN-like, but predicting at full resolution. What BiFPN would add: (a) a bottom-up pass, useless for a single full-resolution output unless followed by another top-down pass; (b) learned scalar fusion weights, +0.45 AP in the source paper, well below anything that would clear our +-0.39 ft noise floor by analogy; (c) uniform narrow width with depthwise convs, the real source of its FLOP savings. Point (c) is not specific to BiFPN. Our up-blocks run at the skip width (384/192/96), so a 'narrow U-Net' (up-block width capped at 64-128) gets the same saving with a one-line change. Correction to repo notes: kaggle_1st_place/CLAUDE.md says the decoder parts hold ~0.05M parameters. That holds only for the full-resolution parts (full_up_block + out + stem ~0.05M). The three up-blocks hold ~4.07M (3.10/0.78/0.19M at convnext_small), about 7.6% of the 53.6M model and about 10 GMAC. So there is some width to prune in the mid-level decoder, contrary to that note, but the time is still dominated by resolution. Resolution warning: with stem_stride (2,4) along (MD, TVT), even the finest encoder map is already 1/4 on the TVT (class) axis (100 of 400 levels). EfficientDet-style heads predict at P2/P3 or coarser, so any BiFPN variant that drops the full-resolution stem path would violate the 2:1 rule, which cost 0.9 ft per halving in the 2nd-place workspace. The shipped design ('big encoder + pruned decoder') already reflects the BiFPN lesson of spending little on the neck.
proposed_experiment: Only worth running as a cheap falsification test. (1) Implement unet_decoder in {'unet' (default), 'unet_narrow', 'bifpn'} in experiments/bilzard/seq_NN_pretrained_unet.py. 'unet_narrow' is BilinearResUpBlock2d with out_ch = min(skip_ch, W) and W = 64 or 128. 'bifpn' projects each stage map to W with a 1x1 conv, runs 2 BiFPN layers (top-down + bottom-up, fast normalised fusion, depthwise-separable 3x3 + BN + SiLU), then takes the finest node (the 1/2 MD x 1/4 TVT level) into the unchanged to_full_resolution -> full_up_block(stem_skip) -> out path. Expose deep_sup_stage_channels = (W, W, W, emb_dim) so deep supervision in seq_NN_models.py:613 still works. Add a recipe flag in seq_NN_cfg.py; reuse the cnx_tiny recipe otherwise. (2) Timing first, no training: in-model CUDA-event timing at 345x400, fp16, batch 1 for all three decoders, with convnext_tiny and fastvit_sa12. If 'bifpn' is not faster than 'unet_narrow', stop: the fusion topology then brings no efficiency. (3) Accuracy: 60-epoch screen of unet vs unet_narrow vs bifpn at W=64 on convnext_tiny, same seed and data. Compare pooled holdout RMSE with the existing robust_compare against the +-0.39 ft single-run noise floor, and also per-column NLL to catch calibration changes. Go to 150 epochs only if bifpn beats unet_narrow by more than 0.39 ft or matches baseline RMSE with at least 15% lower measured latency. (4) Ablate weighted fusion off (plain sum) to attribute any gain. Control run: the current cnx_tiny_ep150 (4.90 ft test-picked) and a fresh 60-epoch baseline.
implementation_effort: Low-medium. About 150 lines for a BiFPN module over 4 levels with odd spatial sizes (200x87, 100x43 ... need size-matched interpolation or pooling in the bottom-up pass, not a fixed stride of 2). 'unet_narrow' is a few lines. Deep-supervision plumbing and recipe flags add a little.
gpu_cost: Timing screen: minutes. Each 60-epoch convnext_tiny screen costs about the same as the existing 60-epoch baselines on the RTX 5060 laptop (8 GB). Three decoders plus one fusion ablation is about 4 screen runs. Memory is lower than the current decoder at W=64. [uncertain: exact hours per run depend on the current recipe's epoch time, not re-measured here]
distillation_compatibility: Fully compatible: the output posterior format is unchanged, so FastViT-student KD on output posteriors works unmodified. A narrower decoder is a natural extra lever for the student's latency.
error_correlation_with_ours: Expected to be highly correlated with the baseline, since encoder, inputs, loss and decode are identical and only the mid-level fusion topology differs. Little value as a separate blend or gate member; seed averaging would likely give similar diversity.
risk: (1) No mechanism aimed at our dominant errors, which need more evidence or better calibration, not better fusion. (2) The evidence base is detection and 1/4-resolution segmentation. The gains are small (+0.3 to +0.45 AP for the topology and weighting parts) and would sit well inside our +-0.39 ft noise floor. (3) Resolution trap: a detection-style BiFPN predicts at P2-P3; dropping the full-resolution path would cost ~0.9 ft per halving under the 2:1 rule. (4) FLOPs are not wall clock here: depthwise-separable repeated fusion is memory-bound, and EfficientNet-B3 is already slower than convnext_tiny in this repo. A lower-FLOP BiFPN may not be faster. (5) Architecture swaps have repeatedly failed at 60 epochs (axial attention, RAFT refinement, AcfNet target), and MobileOne showed capacity cuts below ~10M hurt. The model is data-limited above ~28M, so decoder capacity changes are unlikely to matter much either way. (6) Deep-supervision heads would have to be re-wired, a source of silent bugs.
notes: Verdict on the teammate proposal: the 'lower FLOPs' part is plausible but not specific to BiFPN. Narrowing the existing up-blocks gives the same saving and must be the control. The 'lower RMSE' part has no supporting evidence for full-resolution dense regression. EfficientDet's own segmentation result predicts at 1/4 resolution and confounds a backbone change. Weighted fusion is a ~0.45 AP effect in detection, and fast versus softmax fusion makes no measurable difference (Table 6). Semantic FPN (Kirillov et al. 2019) uses top-down only, because for a single dense output the bottom-up pass has nowhere to deliver its information. A web-search snippet (source not verified) reports BiFPN sitting outside the preferred accuracy/parameter trade-off in a medical-imaging neck ablation [uncertain]. RevBiFPN (MLSys 2023) is a reversible, memory-saving BiFPN backbone and is relevant only if training memory becomes the constraint. Cheaper directions with a mechanism behind them are covered elsewhere: B01 (IGEV++ multi-range cost volumes for large shift vs fine detail), B09 (calibration), B10 (prefix-based drift correction). Side finding for CLAUDE.md: the '~0.05M decoder parameters' statement should read '~0.05M in the full-resolution decoder parts; ~4.1M in the three mid-level up-blocks'.
